I’m a huge fan of the first Helldivers, but since I prefer an isometric perspective over first or third-person views, I wasn't in a rush to buy it and waited for a price drop. After two years of waiting, the biggest discount I saw was only 25%, so I finally bought it. Because of this, I missed out on all the controversies surrounding the game - I didn't personally experience things like weapon nerfs. I bought the game two years after its release and have been playing it quite regularly for the past six months.

I have to admit that the transition from the first Helldivers to a third/first-person perspective was handled really well. It has basically everything the original had, plus more. In addition to the main missions, there are now optional missions and so-called "Points of Interest". This time, strong opponents appear not only after weak patrols raise the alarm, but also at key locations on the map. There’s a variety of missions, planets, weather effects and so on. Plus, after two and a half years, there is far more unlockable content than in the first game. Moreover, the game is constantly being developed, so new missions, enemies, or Warbonds appear from time to time. It’s also worth mentioning the combat itself - like in the first game, it’s quite realistic (for example, you can't shoot while looking at the map on your wrist). The weak-point and dismemberment system is brilliantly executed, especially against larger enemies - you can often destroy specific parts of their armor or blow off their limbs. Honestly, since I started playing this game, going back to older shooters that lack these mechanics just isn't as fun for me as it used to be.

There are a few downsides, though. For me, the biggest one is the time limit - something that wasn't in the first game. I really don't understand why it was introduced, because it certainly doesn't make the game any more fun. After watching some gameplay and seeing how epic everything looked, I worked up the courage to message a cute guy I knew about the game to ask him for his thoughts. I play Helldivers on PC with mouse and keyboard controls, and almost exclusively play with my friends. The few times we have accidentally used the SOS beacon, the randoms that have joined have been super chill. I love the memes and energy of the playerbase. That was the biggest thing that drew me to keep playing the game. Normally, shooters turn me off due to how competitive, stressful, and toxic they can get. But Helldivers is a fun time and relaxing even at high difficulties (once you know what you are doing). This game started off incredibly strong in 2024. Seriously, incredibly strong. Warbonds were actually something to look forward to, updates were exciting, the community was active, and it genuinely felt like Helldivers 2 had an amazing future ahead of it.

Now? It feels like Arrowhead has shot themselves in the foot so many times that it would honestly be easier to ask when they haven't.

Bad balance decisions, questionable updates, bugs, things getting broken that worked perfectly fine before, and some absolutely horrible performance. For a game that has been out this long, the performance problems are ridiculous. Frame drops, stutters, inconsistent performance, and updates that somehow seem capable of making the game run worse instead of better.

Then there's the actual mission structure.

Operations can take over an hour to complete, especially when you're doing multiple missions back-to-back, and the amount of medals you get for that time investment feels terrible. You can spend more than an hour completing an entire operation and walk away wondering why you even bothered. The reward doesn't feel remotely proportional to the amount of time you're expected to put in.

Long missions aren't automatically a problem when the rewards make the time investment worthwhile. Helldivers 2 often doesn't.

And then there's weapon leveling.

Weapon leveling takes FOREVER. Getting a weapon all the way to max level feels like an unnecessary grind stretched out for the sake of being a grind. If you want to fully upgrade multiple weapons, you're looking at a ridiculous amount of time doing the same content over and over again just to finish leveling them.

Experimenting with different weapons should be one of the fun parts of the game, but when maxing out a single weapon takes so long, it starts discouraging you from trying other things. Instead of progression feeling satisfying, it feels painfully slow.

Helldivers 2's greatest flaw is that it punishes players for taking it seriously.

its unpredictable physics and haphazard balancing will either be a source of silly fun or massive frustration depending on what your mindset as a player is. If you want a goofy game to play with friends, it's perfect; if you want a tough but fair TPS experience, you'll be pulling your hair out.

With that said, it has serious issues that will impact players regardless of their skill level, playtime or monetary investment:

[h3] Rough onboarding [/h3]
If you're new to the game or haven't played it for a while, getting back into it is rough. There are currently 26 warbonds, 25 of which cost money. New players do get plenty of guns and stratagems in the base game, but playing on higher difficulties almost requires some hyper specific bits of gear that will necessitate ingame purchases. Technically you can get ingame currency randomly by playing the game, but anyone trying to convince you that you can buy warbonds through that alone is either lying or willing/able to play the game like it's a part time job.

[h3] Excessive nerfs [/h3]
A term that has birthed endless debates around this game is the "grunt fantasy". Essentially, the developers don't want their players to feel like unkillable supersoldiers, as that would undermine the game's themes and tone. This trend started with weapon nerfs and eventually turned into significant gameplay alterations. Players were made unable to respawn on elevated surfaces to discourage camping, stratagem beacons became harder to place reliably, secondary weapons became wildly inaccurate... In a strictly PvE game, limiting player agency this aggressively is uncalled for.

In an ideal world, i'd love to see them reverse these gameplay changes as well as make older warbonds cheaper, or at least allow players to buy warbond items individually at an increased price.

Helldivers 2 and its developer, Arrowhead, are a tragic, but fascinating case study in live service and community mismanagement.

I have been present for most of this game's lifetime and have witnessed:
- The unnecessary and incessant nerfs to weapons just because they were being used
- The gutting of fun functionality on the altar of "balance" (see how the Flamethrower worked at launch vs the Freedom's Flame patch)
- The releasing of content that has clearly not been tested. This has not improved to this day
- The promise of a community or propaganda commander test branch in order to improve the quality of content before release. This has not materialised to this day
- The railroaded galactic war campaign. If you think we have agency in this game to shape the campaign, you are a fool
- The abandoning of features like weapon customisation and meaningful ways to use samples
- The repeated promises by the developer that are never realised
- The bugs that haven't been resolved in almost 3 years
- The bugs that have been fixed and then reintroduced in a later patch. It's either incompetence or maliciousness, take your pick
- The reinvigoration of the game through mods. Mods that fixed the games most obnoxious bugs and pain points, as well as adding new features and customisation
- The subsequent destruction of the modding scene for the game. Perhaps they couldn't let it continue as quality of life mods like the Vanilla Plus Megapack's existence directly contradicted their own statements about fixes they claim to be working on... for almost 6 months

To try and understand why any of this has happened at all is to try and understand madness.
